title: Reference modification WS-FIELD(3:5) — 1-based start, length (NOT end); reading and writing both work
sourceContent:
IDENTIFICATION DIVISION.
       PROGRAM-ID. REF-MOD.
       DATA DIVISION.
       WORKING-STORAGE SECTION.
       01  WS-LINE    PIC X(80).
      *> WS-LINE(3:5) means: start at byte 3 (1-based), take 5 bytes.
      *> NOT 'bytes 3 through 5' -- that would only be 3 chars.
      *> Reading produces a 5-character value; the same expression
      *> on the LHS overwrites those 5 bytes in place. A Java port
      *> using String.substring(2, 7) is correct but the off-by-one
      *> conversion is a common bug.
       PROCEDURE DIVISION.
       MAIN.
           MOVE "hello" TO WS-LINE(3:5).
           STOP RUN.
notes: The (start:length) syntax is unusual — most languages use (start, end). The off-by-one trap on the length side is silent and common. The lvalue form is the major port challenge: Java String is immutable.
